Let \(m=2^n\). The answer is
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/\mathbb Q)\cong C_{2^n}\rtimes (\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times,
\]
where \((\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times\) acts on \(C_{2^n}\) by multiplication. Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/\mathbb Q)
\cong \operatorname{AGL}_1(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z),
\]
the group of affine maps
\[
t\mapsto at+b,\qquad a\in(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times,\ b\in\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z.
\]

For \(n=1\), this is just \(C_2\).

Let
\[
a=\frac{\ell^2+1}{\ell}=\ell+\ell^{-1}.
\]
The key identity is that if \(x=z+z^{-1}\), then
\[
f(x)=x^2-2=z^2+z^{-2},
\]
and hence
\[
f^{\circ n}(x)=z^{2^n}+z^{-2^n}.
\]
Thus \(f^{\circ n}(x)=a\) is equivalent to
\[
z^{m}+z^{-m}=\ell+\ell^{-1}.
\]
So
\[
z^m=\ell \quad\text{or}\quad z^m=\ell^{-1}.
\]
Let \(\alpha=\ell^{1/m}\) and \(\zeta=\zeta_m\). Then the roots are
\[
x_i=\alpha\zeta^i+\alpha^{-1}\zeta^{-i},
\qquad i\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z.
\]
Therefore all roots lie in
\[
F=\mathbb Q(\alpha,\zeta_m).
\]

Conversely, the splitting field \(K_n\) contains all \(x_i\). The field \(F/\mathbb Q\) is Galois, and every automorphism of \(F\) has the form
\[
\sigma_{a,b}(\zeta)=\zeta^a,\qquad
\sigma_{a,b}(\alpha)=\zeta^b\alpha,
\]
with \(a\in(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^\times\), \(b\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z\). Such an automorphism sends
\[
x_i\mapsto x_{b+ai}.
\]
If it fixes every root \(x_i\), then \(x_{b+ai}=x_i\) for all \(i\). But \(x_j=x_i\) forces \(j=i\), since otherwise
\[
\alpha\zeta^j+\alpha^{-1}\zeta^{-j}
=
\alpha\zeta^i+\alpha^{-1}\zeta^{-i}
\]
would imply either \(\zeta^j=\zeta^i\), or \(\alpha^2\) is a root of unity, impossible because \(\alpha^2>1\). Hence \(b=0\) and \(a=1\). So no nontrivial automorphism of \(F\) fixes \(K_n\), and because \(F/\mathbb Q\) and \(K_n/\mathbb Q\) are Galois, we get
\[
K_n=F.
\]

It remains only to identify the Galois group. Since \(\ell\) is an odd prime, \(\ell\) is not a square in \(\mathbb Q(\zeta_m)\): that cyclotomic field is ramified only at \(2\), while \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{\ell})\) is ramified at \(\ell\). Hence \(X^m-\ell\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb Q(\zeta_m)\), so the choices
\[
\alpha\mapsto \zeta^b\alpha,\qquad \zeta\mapsto \zeta^a
\]
are independent. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/\mathbb Q)
=
\{\sigma_{a,b}:a\in(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^\times,\ b\in\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z\},
\]
with composition
\[
(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',\,b+ab').
\]

Thus, with \(m=2^n\),
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/\mathbb Q)\cong
\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z\rtimes(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^\times.}
\]
